result.title: FinVision: Multimodal AI for Visualizing Financial Narratives
result.summary: Financial narratives contain rich information about firms' performance and business conditions. Conventional text analysis often summarizes this information into numerical representations, which may not fully preserve the dynamic structure described in the narrative. In this study, we develop FinVision, a domain-specific multimodal generative model that translates financial narratives into visual representations of contemporaneous market dynamics. Using 87,940 paired observations of Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) disclosures and stock price charts, FinVision learns the average relationship between a firm's narrative account of a fiscal year and its stock-price dynamics over the same period. Given an MD&A alone, the trained model generates a text-implied stock chart, extending financial text analysis beyond numerical representations toward text-to-visual generation. We validate FinVision in two ways. First, held-out tests show that the model generates stock-chart representations that closely resemble observed charts and outperform direct LLM prompting, general-purpose text-to-image models, and the same architecture without financial-domain adaptation. Second, we examine the economic validity of the generated representations by comparing text-implied and observed stock charts. The resulting discrepancy is systematically associated with weaker investor responses around subsequent 10-K filings and with worse subsequent market and operating outcomes. Overall, our findings show how domain-adapted multimodal generative AI can create a new visual representation of financial text and provide an additional modality for studying business communication.

AI.brief_summary: 该文构建金融领域多模态生成模型 FinVision，用约 8.8 万条 MD&A 文本与同期股价走势图配对数据训练，使模型仅凭管理层讨论文本生成「文本隐含股价图」，并检验其与真实图表的接近程度及与后续市场反应、经营结果的经济关联。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于金融文本到图表生成的领域应用，既未涉及 VLM 推理期的视觉信息保留与 latent 状态，也未提出可供核查的状态更新、证据筛选或停止决策线索，与研究主线缺少实质联系。
